issues.description: The `a.root` fast-path lacks a stated invariant explaining the parent-relationship semantics.
issues.detail: The change reinterprets `root` from a bool to a `*namespace.Namespace` carrying the policy's owning namespace, and gates the fast-path on `ns.HasParent(a.root)`. The invariant — 'an ACL bearing a root policy from namespace N authorizes any request whose context namespace is a descendant of N (inclusive?)' — is not stated in code. A reader cannot tell from the comment whether `HasParent` is reflexive (does root-ns root token authorize root-ns requests?). NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT.

issues.description: `HasParent` semantics are load-bearing for the root-token authorization path but unaudited in this diff.
issues.detail: The entire security model of namespace-owned root tokens now depends on `ns.HasParent(a.root)` returning true exactly when authorization should be granted. If `HasParent` is strict (excludes self), a root-ns root token may stop authorizing root-ns requests; if it accepts string-prefix matches (`ns1` vs `ns10`), it over-grants. The test only covers `Path: 'ns1'` with no ID, which is not representative. UNDER-AUDITED.

issues.description: `NamespaceSealed` is a stub that unconditionally returns false and is already wired into a caller.
issues.detail: `(*Core).NamespaceSealed` returns `false` with a TODO, but `ListAllNamespaces` (per the PR description) is already adjusted to consult it. Shipping a stub that silently lies about sealed state is a correctness hazard: any future caller added before the seal manager lands will get wrong answers with no compile-time signal. At minimum, panic in non-production builds or return `ErrNotImplemented` so callers cannot accidentally depend on it.

issues.description: `AdjustErrorStatusCode` refactor changes from independent checks to mutually exclusive switch cases.
issues.detail: The old code ran each `if` independently, so a single error could match multiple branches and the last one would win. The new `switch` short-circuits on first match. This is likely an improvement, but it is a behavioral change not called out: e.g. an error wrapping both `ErrSealed` and an `HTTPCodedError` previously had its code overwritten by the coded error; now the sealed branch wins. The ordering needs an explicit comment justifying precedence.

issues.description: `NSTokenLength = TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID` is opaque and abuses string indexing for a constant.
issues.detail: Per the PR description, `NSTokenLength` is defined as `TokenLen + "."[1] + nsID`. `"."[1]` indexes past the end of a one-byte string — if literally written this way it is a compile error or wrong constant. Even if it is `"."[0]` (the byte value 46) being added as a length, that conflates an ASCII codepoint with a character count. This needs to be `TokenLen + len(".") + nsIDLen` with named constants. NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT and likely ASYMPTOTICALLY-WRONG-as-written.

issues.description: Test `testACLRoot` constructs a namespace with only `Path: "ns1"` and empty ID, masking the real invariant.
issues.detail: The child-namespace test creates `&namespace.Namespace{Path: "ns1"}` with no ID, then asserts that a root-namespace context is rejected. This tests the wrong axis: real namespaces have IDs, and `HasParent` likely compares IDs/paths in ways this fixture doesn't exercise. Add cases for deep nesting (`ns1/ns2`), sibling rejection (`ns1` root token vs `ns2` request), and ID-based parentage. UNDER-AUDITED test coverage.

review.summary: The PR makes a structurally sound generalization — turning ACL.root from a bool into the owning namespace pointer — but ships without stating the load-bearing invariant ("root policy in N authorizes requests in descendants of N") and without auditing the `HasParent` semantics it now depends on. A stub `NamespaceSealed` returning false is already wired into callers, which is a correctness hazard until the seal manager lands. The `AdjustErrorStatusCode` refactor changes independent checks into a precedence-ordered switch without comment. Test coverage for the new child-namespace authorization path uses a degenerate namespace fixture and does not exercise sibling rejection or deep nesting. Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED with NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the root fast-path; recommend annotating the invariant, hardening the stub, and broadening tests before merge.
